stem: A developer runs `tsc --noEmitOnError app.ts` on a project file containing a type error. Prior to this command, an older `app.js` file already existed in the target directory. What happens to `app.js` upon executing the compiler command?
options: app.js is overwritten with comments detailing the type errors detected during compilation.
app.js is not generated or updated because --noEmitOnError halts emission when type-checking errors are encountered.
app.js is updated with transpiled JavaScript because type errors never prevent output emission.
app.js is deleted immediately by the compiler to prevent outdated JavaScript from executing.
objective: Compile TypeScript source files via the command line using tsc and verify that --noEmitOnError suppresses output when errors occur

options: The property .length is not recognized unless the array element type is explicitly defined.
Functions must always declare an explicit return type whenever --noImplicitAny is enabled.
The parameter items has no type annotation and cannot be inferred, causing TypeScript to implicitly fall back to any, which --noImplicitAny rejects.
Parameters that access collection properties must declare a generic interface constraint.
objective: Identify type errors triggered by --noImplicitAny and --strictNullChecks when handling unannotated variables and nullish values

stem: A function signature is defined as `function getLength(str: string | null): number`. When `--strictNullChecks` is enabled, why does the expression `return str.length;` inside the function body trigger a compiler error?
options: TypeScript requires undefined to always be included whenever null is specified in a parameter union type.
Under --strictNullChecks, null has its own distinct type and cannot be used where a concrete value of type string is expected without checking first.
Enabling --strictNullChecks completely forbids union types containing null from being passed as function parameters.
The string type in TypeScript does not have a built-in .length property unless asserted with the as operator.
objective: Identify type errors triggered by --noImplicitAny and --strictNullChecks when handling unannotated variables and nullish values
